shared-edit apps/Model Plane/docs/decisions/ledger.md: append at the end of the file two entries. Entry 1 heading `## Memory control state and one decision gate (WS07-S1, 2026-10-26)`; body: The owner's memory is on, paused or off, stored on user_memory_controls beside the extraction watermark. A pause stops new memory without deleting anything: rows stay visible and deletable, and a resume moves the watermark forward, so nothing written while paused is mined later. off also hides the owner's rows. Org-owned rows stay readable while the owner is paused or off, and an organization that turns memory off suppresses them too. memory_control::resolve folds the owner's state, the organization policy and the ZDR posture into one decision with closed reasons, and every session-core reader and writer takes that decision instead of reading the state itself, because a second reader that checks the state alone is how a paused user is remembered anyway. The control tables hold state and counts only, never content. Status: implemented in part (the session-core gate is WS07-S1, partial; the capability-core memory writer waits on WS07-S5). Entry 2 heading `## Learned skills are owner-scoped disabled proposals (WS07-S7, 2026-10-26)`; body: The review never enables or shares a skill. It writes a proposed row with scope user and enabled false, owned by the user whose run it came from, and session-core forces that shape whatever the reviewer returns. The conflict key is (org, scope, owner, name), so one user's proposal cannot overwrite another's, and a conflict never re-enables a row an owner or admin disabled. Only the owner's accept makes a proposal usable; an organization copy is an admin's explicit promotion. Auto-accept stays off until live evidence from the seeded eval exists (WS07-S10). Why: the reviewer reads a customer conversation and its reply is untrusted model output, so only the owner can make a learned skill take effect; the review's spend is bounded per owner and per organization per day by the cost controls, which are off unless switched on and skip every review while no counter store is wired. Status: implemented in part (the proposal shape is WS07-S7, done; accept, reject and undo are WS07-S8 and S9, partial).

results.notes: Built WS09-S6 behind VITE_CHAT_PARALLEL_THREAD_LOAD (exact 'true' via parallelThreadLoadEnabled in chat-client.ts, read at call time, default off). Flag off keeps the same request order (session, then transcript, then messages); only a synchronous local-snapshot read moved ahead of the session request. Flag on: the messages read starts with the session read; the transcript starts with them only when the local snapshot has no turns, and is skipped on a warm open once the session is found, with cachedUpdatedAt taken from the session when the messages read returns messages (the same value the transcript would carry; history.rs sets it from the same session). listChatThreads single-flights concurrent callers under the flag and returns each caller its own array. Turn arrays are equal flag-on and flag-off in the cold and warm fixture tests. ZDR: reads only; no write path changed. The flag stays off in every committed default.
